Fri

Jul 31Medium-low confidenceoutbound · 06:00–22:00 ET
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KLZU observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. KLZU has no TAF station, so KPDK is used as a proxy. It is the strongest flight-category evidence this page can show. Beyond the TAF horizon of about 30 hours; no TAF exists at this range for any station.NWS-hrNWS hourly gridpoint forecast — the National Weather Service digital forecast for the grid cell containing KLZU, updated through the day and reaching about 156 hours. It gives hour-by-hour sky, wind and precipitation probability, and it is the spine of the change windows on this board. The NWS hourly gridpoint forecast reaches this day.NWS-dayNWS day/night outlook — the same National Weather Service grid summarised into day and night halves, reaching about 168 hours. Coarser than the hourly product but it covers one day further, so this page uses it only to describe spans the hourly forecast cannot reach. Not needed: this day is already covered by the finer-resolution hourly gridpoint forecast.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued by the National Weather Service four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this page uses it to corroborate the flight category. Beyond the GFS MAV MOS horizon of about 72 hours, or no MAV row carried both a ceiling and a visibility for this day.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This page shows it only as a flagged outlook and never promotes it into a short-range category. This day is already covered by finer-resolution sources.GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KLZU this run.

Extended outlook summary

.. (This afternoon through Wednesday) Issued at 248 PM EDT Tue Jul 28 2026 Folks, it's warm out there. — .. (Thursday morning through next Monday) Issued at 248 PM EDT Tue Jul 28 2026 By Wed night the cold front that moved into the area in the short term will still be moving south through the state moving into South GA/N FL by Thu morning.

Short term

.. (This afternoon through Wednesday) Issued at 248 PM EDT Tue Jul 28 2026 Folks, it's warm out there. Heat indices are into the triple digits across much of north and central Georgia this afternoon with the ATL airport sitting at a just ~lovely~ 105 F heat index as of this writing. Temperatures are in the 90s and dewpoints are in the 70s. The good news up front is that some relief from the heat is on the way, though it will take a day or two to filter into the area. The only other things of note is that things likely look a little hazy up above - wildfire smoke from the Pacific NW is filtering around the ridge and being carried by the jet over us. Another burst of this is expected to move in later tonight per "smoke allowing" convective guidance, though again this should mostly remain well above us and not impact us on the ground. Other weather story we are monitoring is convective chances later tonight. I honestly wish I could say we had a bit more certainty given we are only a few hours from when storms may push in, but model guidance remains boom or bust, with more bust than boom. Aloft we have a shortwave embedded in the jet that has given us a nice jet streak within the NW flow around the large ridge over the central CONUS. Front associated with this has already started to fire some convection in KY and WV that -should- be the main player for us later tonight. These storms are expected to congeal into a line of storms that pushes south and eventually southeast, moving into the area from NC/TN after accelerating ahead of the frontal boundary. Where the big uncertainty begins is as it approaches the state - many CAMs completely dissipate the system, in some cases before it even reaches the border. Others hold it together briefly into the state but have it quickly fall apart after that. This is certainly possible, given the system should outrun both forcing and better shear and run into our area after sunset, meaning surface based parcels will be more challenging to get going. However, there are some biases here to consider, especially with over mixing of moisture, which could be having an outsized impact on the convective coverage of these models. The other side of the coin is the REFS (RRFS ensemble), which does show ~40% of members holding storms together into north Georgia, and keeping even 20-30% chances into the Atlanta metro. So, with all that said, the current forecast leans towards that 30- 40% chance of seeing something across northern Georgia. Given we will still have ~3000 J/kg of instability to work with ahead of the line well into the overnight hours, storms may remain vigorous with some isolated damaging wind gusts possible. A Slight Risk remains in effect for NE GA with a Marginal Risk extending into the metro and the rest of N GA. Relatively cooler and drier air is expected to begin filtering into northern Georgia by early morning tomorrow. The diurnal cycle will slow down the progression of the front into the area through the afternoon, so looks like portions of central Georgia will have to wait another day to get relief from the heat. While heat indices should "only" reach into the 90s across north Georgia and the metro on Wednesday, they will go soaring once again into the triple digits across portions of central Georgia. Heat Advisories will likely be needed once again, with issuance later tonight after the current advisories expire. Some afternoon thunderstorms will be possible across central Georgia during the afternoon ahead of the stalled outflow boundary from tonight's system. This could put a damper on the worst of the heat, especially if coverage is more than expected.

Long term

.. (Thursday morning through next Monday) Issued at 248 PM EDT Tue Jul 28 2026 By Wed night the cold front that moved into the area in the short term will still be moving south through the state moving into South GA/N FL by Thu morning. This boundary stalls near the FL/GA border but it does usher in some drier air which should keep North and Central GA precipitation free through Friday night. Temps are not expected to cool to much Thu/Fri with high temps still expected in the upper 80s to middle 90s but the Apparent T (feels like temps) will be much lower. By Sat the next frontal boundary moving east out of the lower to mid MS river valley moves into W GA just before daybreak. The main low pressure center moves east into western KY at the same time. With the close proximity of the low center to NW GA this frontal boundary should stay fairly organized as it moves into the region. The current forecast models show this front stalling across E/SE GA and the Carolinas through Tues keeping the area in moist S to SW flow through day 7. This will keep precip chances elevated through day 7.

Editorial #1 KAVL VFR Asheville Muni, NC, US · cool mountain escapeETE0h49Dist112 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KAVL observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KAVL this run.

Editorial #8 KTRI VFR Bristol/Tri-Cities Arpt, TN, US · Tri-Cities TN/VAETE1h11Dist168 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KTRI observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KTRI this run.

Editorial #13 KGKT VFR Gatlinburg-Pigeon Forge Arpt, TN, US · Smokies/GatlinburgETE0h50Dist114 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KGKT observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KTYS is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KGKT this run.

Editorial #14 KSHD VFR Staunton/Shenandoah Valley Rgnl, VA, US · Shenandoah valleyETE2h25Dist355 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSHD observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KCHO is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KSHD this run.

Editorial #3 KSSI VFR Brunswick/McKinnon St Simons Arpt, GA, US · St Simons beachETE1h29Dist214 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSSI observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KSSI this run.

METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KFIN observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KDAB is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KFIN this run.

Editorial #6 KCRE VFR North Myrtle Beach/Grand Strand Arpt, SC, US · N Myrtle BeachETE1h49Dist261 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KCRE observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KMYR is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KCRE this run.

Editorial #11 KCRG VFR Jacksonville/Executive at Craig Arpt, FL, US · Jacksonville ExecETE1h45Dist252 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KCRG observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KCRG this run.

Editorial #16 KPNS VFR Pensacola Intl, FL, US · Pensacola (Class C)ETE1h51Dist267 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KPNS observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KPNS this run.

Editorial #17 KDAB VFR Daytona Beach Intl, FL, US · Daytona Beach (Class C)ETE2h13Dist324 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KDAB observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KDAB this run.

METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSPG observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KPIE is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KSPG this run.

Editorial #23 KSRQ VFR Sarasota-Bradenton Intl, FL, US · Sarasota-BradentonETE2h43Dist402 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSRQ observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: RATE_LIMITED), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

Gulf West

Editorial #18 KJKA VFR Gulf Shores/Edwards Arpt, AL, US · Gulf Shores ALETE2h01Dist291 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KJKA observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KJKA this run.

Editorial #27 KOPF VFR Miami/Opa Locka Arpt, FL, US · Miami-Opa LockaETE3h30Dist521 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KOPF observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KOPF this run.

Editorial #28 KHPN MVFR White Plains/Westchester Cnty, NY, US · White Plains NYETE4h18Dist647 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KHPN observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KHPN this run.

3 · Hazard feeds & regional observations

Unfiltered hazard feeds (not route-geometry screened): 13 SIGMET records, 26 G-AIRMET records, 5 CWA records. Regional current observations (not corridor forecasts): Gulf East: category unavailable at KTPF; Long-range: MVFR at KHPN.
Scope: Hazard counts are raw feed totals and have not been filtered against a proposed route, altitude, or time. Airport flight categories are current point observations, not corridor forecasts.

4 · Planning gates

  • Evidence gate: an unavailable, stale, or out-of-horizon source is unknown — never treat it as favorable.
  • Weather gate: compare current observations and valid-period forecasts with personal ceiling, visibility, convection, wind, and crosswind minimums.
  • Route gate: screen the actual route, altitude, and time against official hazard products; feed totals on this page are not route-filtered.
  • Operations gate: verify NOTAMs, TFRs, runway conditions, fuel, aircraft performance, daylight, and alternates.

5 · ForeFlight manual cross-check (before flight)

  • ☐ Official briefing matches these go/no-go windows
  • ☐ Prog charts / radar / satellite trend agrees with convection timing
  • ☐ Winds & temps aloft along actual route (may shift ETE)
  • ☐ NOTAMs & TFRs — airport-scoped NMS records may be shown, but route-wide/TFR coverage is not included; pull a fresh official briefing for departure, destination, and alternates
  • ☐ Runway condition / length / closures at destination & alternate
  • ☐ Weight & balance + performance at forecast density altitude (heat!)
  • ☐ File & brief in ForeFlight; confirm fuel stops if long-range

★ Features

Available now

  • Per-source state, validity horizon, and target-date coverage for every destination
  • Explicit unavailable/out-of-horizon target cells; no static weather fallback
  • Per-airport expandable detail — current observations, covered forecasts, dep/dest METAR temperatures
  • Four-day KLZU change-window board with four outbound/return planning alternatives
  • Source-labelled TAF/MOS flight-category guidance only when a source interval actually covers the planned window — a day with no covering interval shows an explicit unavailable/out-of-horizon state instead of a category, never an implied one
  • Timed NWS weather, wind-favored runway (magnetic, from each airport's own runways), gust, and material crosswind context wherever the forecast supplies them
  • Raw METAR/TAF + data-sources dropdown per airport
  • FAA Airport Status & Delays with known, unsupported, and unavailable states
  • Best-effort 100LL fuel prices
  • Auto-refreshed about 4x a day by an hourly scheduler that republishes once 6 h have passed since the last publish, so refresh times drift; the last-updated stamp is exact and the next-run stamp is an estimate
  • Quick links (Flight Circle, ForeFlight, FlightAware) + Feedback
  • FAA chart-cycle stamp (current VFR Sectional + Chart Supplement)
  • Download PDF — print-ready, color-preserving (semantic colors kept on paper)
  • Deterministic evidence-backed page; external AI aviation prose is withheld pending a validated evidence schema, so the executive-summary region shows an explicit pending-feature placeholder instead of generated text
  • Model-labeled MOS target-window outlook per airport (Iowa State GFS with conditional GFS Extended/MEX), with runtime and validity horizon shown
  • Expandable NWS FFC pattern summary and extended outlook inside the KLZU board
  • Per-airport chart links: SkyVector & AirNav/Chart Supplement (deep links)
  • FAA NMS Pre-Production (sandbox) NOTAM adapter with explicit per-airport source states; active on this page with non-operational Pre-Production test data, and never a substitute for an official briefing
  • Full run archive: run_manifest.json with all data + provenance log
